name: Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd
title: Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd - 500038 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Balrampur Chini guided ~40% average PLA capacity utilisation for Jan-Mar 2027 and held 45.67 lakh quintals of sugar stock at INR 37.19/kg carrying cost.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a tighter-than-expected season with lower production, healthy domestic consumption and ethanol diversion drawing down inventory, which firmed sugar prices to roughly INR 48-49 per kg. Q1 is an off-season quarter with almost no sugar production, so results reflect carrying cost and realisation of inventory from the prior season. The 80,000-tonne PLA plant is on track, with lactic acid commissioning expected in October and PLA in December, and about INR 2,180 crore spent by end-July. Management said it sees no B-heavy or juice diversion next season as a reasonable working assumption, but did not give quantified Q1 financials on the call.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Q1 is off-season with largely no production; 45.67 lakh quintals inventory at INR 37.19/kg carrying cost is seen as a favourable base for upcoming quarters. Some Maizapur distillery costs were retained in sugar, not distillery, in Q1.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: Q1 margins described as resilient, driven by B-heavy and maize-based ethanol with hardly any juice-based sales. Management said distillery costs are not comparable apples-to-apples due to cost allocation to sugar.

segments.name: PLA (new, 80,000 t)
segments.commentary: Lactic acid commissioning targeted October 2026 and PLA December 2026; ~40% average utilisation guided for Jan-Mar 2027, described as a safe expectation with target higher.

guidance_outlook: PLA: lactic acid commissioning around October 2026 and PLA around December 2026, subject to production, quality and timing.
PLA: safe expectation of ~40% average capacity utilisation for January-March 2027; internal target is higher.

FY28 ethanol: management assumes no B-heavy or juice diversion allowed next season and only C-heavy permitted; company has not yet finalised numbers. Expects crushing may reduce slightly in some units but overall targets intact.

Sugar price: management expects a cane price hike and ban on diversion, and believes the net effect will be positive; said closing-stock tightness could normalise by around 1 October 2027, with prices above current levels in coming years.
Clarity on 2026-27 sugar season production expected around end-September 2026.
capex_capacity: 80,000-tonne PLA plant on track; civil work, equipment arrivals and erection underway.
Maizapur distillery equipped for grain-based ethanol (~10 crore litres per analyst's cited figure), and now ready to make sugar as well.
Management said C-heavy-based distillery volumes are fully equipped across all units.
Cane development and varietal balancing identified as key focus areas.
demand_pricing: Domestic sugar prices firmed on tighter inventory; management says the market is assuming closing stock lower than reality.
Management view: 2025-26 closing stock could be meaningfully higher than market assumes; rejected external estimates of a 20 lakh tonne spread as not credible.
Illustrative balance: 31 mt gross production, 29 mt consumption, ~3 mt closing stock; 45-50 lakh tonnes consumption could take stock to normal by 1 October 2027 if diversion is banned.
PLA demand: management cites pan masala/gutka packaging shift after FSSAI-related moves; technical trials positive; outcome expected within 2-3 months; no verified market size given.
Cane sowing area described as flat YoY with better yields expected; Q1 rainfall described as ideal for cane in the company's area.

qa_highlights.question: What distillery volumes are achievable next season if B-heavy and juice diversion are restricted (C-heavy ~10 crore litres, grain ~9-10 crore litres)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no B-heavy or juice diversion is a reasonable assumption and only C-heavy would be allowed; the analyst's C-heavy estimate was 'not too much off the mark', with numbers still being reworked. Grain availability depends on government broken-rice policy expected around September-October.

qa_highlights.question: When will PLA be commissioned and what first-year utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Lactic acid targeted for October and PLA for December 2026; management asked investors not to judge Q1 on PLA and said 3-6 months at best to see the trend. Jan-Mar 2027 guided at ~40% average utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a parallel Balrampur opportunity from the INR 3,000-3,200 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 'definitely yes' if things go right, but described this as a first attempt requiring patience.

qa_highlights.question: Why did distillery margins hold up despite higher transfer pricing, and will they continue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 used mainly B-heavy and maize ethanol with hardly any juice sales. Maizapur costs were retained in sugar, so the comparison is not like-for-like. Management said less B-heavy means more sugar, which should be net positive.

qa_highlights.question: How long before the sugar stock tightness normalises, and what price levels are sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about one year, around 1 October 2027, if diversion is not allowed; he expected prices to stay above current levels in upcoming years.

qa_highlights.question: Would PLA qualify under the proposed rule that pan masala packaging be free of plastic and synthetic polymers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is dynamic and the answer is 'yes and no' pending government clarification.

risks_watch: Government policy on B-heavy/juice diversion and grain-based ethanol, which will drive FY28 distillery volumes.
Cane price hike ahead of the state elections, which could offset higher sugar realisations.
PLA commissioning (October), production start (December) and utilisation against 40% guidance for Jan-Mar 2027; PLA regulatory treatment under pan masala packaging rules.
Sugar production outlook for 2026-27, with the first clarity expected around end-September 2026; El Nino and monsoon risk.
Management's sugar balance-sheet view (closing stock) differs from market estimates; verify once ISMA and government data firm up.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on sugar pricing and PLA prospects, but noticeably cautious on near-term PLA numbers, repeatedly asking analysts not to model Q1 PLA output. Management was evasive on specific FY27 volumes and sugar balance-sheet estimates, and gave no quantified Q1 P&L on the call.

Even if consumption is to move a little, 45 to 50 lakh tonnes, you could see on 1st October 2027.
So, we expect that from January to March we will have quality production which will be sold.
